title: Cardinals vs. Chiefs Live Score & Stats: November 22, 2026 Showdown – CBS Sports Gametracker
body:
Kansas City cemented its place atop the AFC West on Sunday night with a decisive 38‑17 victory over the Arizona Cardinals in Kansas City’s Arrowhead Stadium. Quarterback Patrick Mahomes threw for 327 yards and three touchdowns, two of them finding his longtime target Travis Kelce, while the Chiefs’ ground attack—led by a surprisingly effective running corps—racked up 145 rushing yards and kept the Cardinals’ defense off balance. Arizona, struggling to establish a rhythm on both sides of the ball, managed only a single touchdown, a 12‑yard pass from quarterback Kyler Murray to wideout Marquez Valdes‑White, before the game slipped beyond reach in the second quarter.

The Chiefs’ offensive explosion was anchored by Mahomes’ poise under pressure. After a tentative start that saw the Cardinals open the scoring with a 42‑yard field goal, Mahomes responded with a 23‑yard strike to tight end Logan Thomas, tying the game at 3‑3. From there, Kansas City seized control, stringing together a 14‑0 run that featured a 61‑yard touchdown pass to Kelce and a 7‑yard rush by rookie running back Jaxon Carter. The Chiefs’ play‑calling displayed a balanced approach, mixing deep vertical shots with a newly emphasized inside‑run game that exploited Arizona’s vulnerable interior line. The Cardinals, accustomed to defending against Mahomes’ aerial prowess, found themselves forced to defend the run—a scenario they have struggled with all season.

Arizona’s offense, which has hovered near the bottom of the league in passing efficiency, never seemed to find a foothold. Murray, who entered the game after a two‑week absence due to a hamstring strain, completed 18 of 29 attempts for 212 yards but threw two interceptions, both of which were returned deep into Cardinals territory. The first pick, a 34‑yard toss intended for wideout DeAndre Hopkins, was snatched by Chiefs safety Nick Bosa and taken to the 10‑yard line, setting up a short-field touchdown that extended Kansas City’s lead to 21‑3. The second interception came late in the third quarter, halting a promising drive that had moved the ball into Chiefs’ red‑zone territory.

Defensively, the Chiefs were equally dominant. Their front seven, anchored by veteran defensive end Chris Jones, generated constant pressure, sacking Murray three times and forcing the Cardinals into hurried throws. The secondary, led by cornerback L'Jarius Sneed, limited Arizona’s receivers to a combined 112 yards, a stark contrast to the 312 yards they allowed to the Chiefs’ passing attack. Kansas City’s opportunistic defense also contributed directly to the score, recovering a fumble on a punt return and returning it for a 27‑yard touchdown that pushed the lead to 31‑7 early in the fourth quarter.

The loss drops the Cardinals to 3‑6 on the season and intensifies scrutiny on head coach Jonathan Gannon’s offensive scheme. Analysts note that Arizona’s inability to adjust to Kansas City’s diversified attack—particularly the unexpected emphasis on inside runs—exposes a broader issue: the Cardinals have struggled to defend the run all year, ranking 28th in rushing yards allowed. If they hope to rebound, Gannon must find a way to protect Murray’s blind side and incorporate quicker, high‑percentage passes that neutralize the Chiefs’ pass rush.

For Kansas City, the win propels them to 10‑0, reinforcing Mahomes’ candidacy for another MVP award and cementing the Chiefs as the team to beat in the AFC. The victory also underscores the emergence of Jaxon Carter, whose 78‑yard burst on the second drive signaled a potential shift toward a more balanced offensive identity. Looking ahead, the Chiefs will face a formidable challenge in Week 15 when they travel to Los Angeles to meet the Chargers, a matchup that could test both their aerial firepower and their newly honed ground game. Arizona, meanwhile, must regroup quickly as they head to Seattle for a crucial divisional battle that could determine whether they finish the season with a chance at a wild‑card berth or settle for a rebuilding year.
